title: The Story of the Persistent Widow
bigIdea: We should always pray and never give up — God loves to hear us and answer.

memoryVerse.text: Jesus said we should always pray and never give up.

moral.lesson: The widow kept on asking and never gave up, and finally even the unkind judge helped her. Jesus said: if a grumpy judge will help someone who keeps asking, then our loving God — who cares about us so much — will surely listen to His children. So we never need to give up on praying.
moral.application: Keep talking to God and never stop praying, even when an answer takes a while. God always hears you, He loves you, and He loves to answer His children.

style: Flat-color children's cartoon storybook illustration, simple rounded shapes, soft warm colors, thick clean black outlines, bright and friendly, gentle lighting, 16:9 landscape composition, no text or words in the image, no letters.
character: the widow: a kind older woman with a gentle face wearing a simple blue robe and a head covering; and the judge: a grumpy man in fancy robes. Keep the widow and the judge looking the same in every picture.

beats.scene: Jesus with brown hair and a beard in a cream robe sits teaching a small group of people outdoors, gesturing kindly as he tells a story. Sunny, peaceful hillside.
text: Jesus wanted to teach His friends something important about prayer.
He wanted them to know that they should always keep praying…
and never, ever give up. So He told them a story.

beats.scene: A kind older woman in a blue robe and head covering stands before a grumpy judge who sits in a fancy chair looking bored and uncaring, turning his head away. A simple courtroom in a Bible-times building.
text: In a certain town there was a judge whose job was to help people. But this judge didn't really care about anyone.
A widow in the town needed his help. She came to him and said, “Please help me! Someone has been unfair to me.”
But the judge just shrugged and ignored her.

beats.scene: The same older woman in the blue robe coming back again and again, shown determined and hopeful, knocking at the judge's door. Maybe shown returning down a path. Bright, determined mood.
text: But the widow did not give up. Not even a little.
She came back the next day, and the next day, and the day after that.
Again and again she asked, “Please help me!” She was patient and she kept on trying.

beats.scene: The grumpy judge throwing up his hands and finally agreeing to help, looking a bit exasperated, while the widow stands hopeful. The judge gestures 'okay, okay!'. Courtroom scene.
text: Finally the judge said to himself, “I don't really care about anyone…
but this woman keeps coming back and she will not give up!
All right — I will help her, just so she will be happy.” And he did!

beats.scene: A warm, glowing scene of a child or person kneeling in happy prayer with hands together, looking up toward a bright, gentle light from the sky. Peaceful and hopeful, full of warmth.
text: Then Jesus explained what the story meant. “Did you see? Even an unkind judge finally helped the woman who kept asking.
How much MORE will our loving God listen to His own children who pray to Him!”
So we should always pray and never give up. God hears us, He loves us, and He loves to answer!
